1: Project PartyRegistryServiceV1 {
2:   database_type: 'PostgreSQL'
3: 
4:   Note: '''
5:     Party Registry Service V1 - bounded context for tenant-scoped civil and legal identity.
6: 
7:     It is the system of record for identity data registered and maintained within
8:     each tenant. It owns Parties, their natural-person or legal-entity details,
9:     nationalities, official identifiers, and the database-managed identification
10:     scheme reference catalog used to normalize and validate those identifiers.
11: 
12:     It does not own customers, suppliers, employees, user accounts, authentication,
13:     authorization, operating organizations, addresses, contacts, subscriptions,
14:     audit storage, tax configuration, ownership structures, beneficial ownership,
15:     or legal/corporate relationship management.
16: 
17:     Other microservices keep party_id as an opaque reference and do not create
18:     foreign keys to this database.
19: 
20:     Country codes are logical references to the Geographic Reference Service,
21:     using ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes, without remote foreign keys.
22: 
23:     Complete identification values are encrypted with authenticated encryption.
24:     Exact lookup and permanent identifier uniqueness use a tenant-isolated
25:     HMAC-SHA-256 fingerprint encoded as exactly 64 uppercase hexadecimal
26:     characters. Within one tenant and Identifier Scheme, the same normalized
27:     identifier value can never be registered more than once, regardless of
28:     lifecycle status.
29: 
30:     Identifier Schemes such as CEDULA, RUC and PASSPORT are database-managed
31:     reference data. Party Registry runtime reads them but does not create, update,
32:     delete or transition them through application use cases or REST endpoints.
33: 
34:     Keycloak authenticates accounts, but it is not the registry of persons.
35:     The relationship between an authenticated subject and party_id belongs to
36:     the Access Management Service.
37: 
38:     Every mutable business table contains created_at, created_by, updated_at and
39:     updated_by. Aggregate roots additionally contain version for optimistic
40:     concurrency control.
41: 
42:     party_outbox_events is infrastructure for reliable publication of tenant-scoped
43:     business events. It does not publish database-schema, Flyway, platform, or
44:     database-managed identifier-scheme catalog changes.
45:   '''

Project PartyRegistryServiceV1 {
  database_type: 'PostgreSQL'

  Note: '''
    Party Registry Service V1 - bounded context for tenant-scoped civil and legal identity.

    It is the system of record for identity data registered and maintained within
    each tenant. It owns Parties, their natural-person or legal-entity details,
    nationalities, official identifiers, and the database-managed identification
    scheme reference catalog used to normalize and validate those identifiers.

    It does not own customers, suppliers, employees, user accounts, authentication,
    authorization, operating organizations, addresses, contacts, subscriptions,
    audit storage, tax configuration, ownership structures, beneficial ownership,
    or legal/corporate relationship management.

    Other microservices keep party_id as an opaque reference and do not create
    foreign keys to this database.

    Country codes are logical references to the Geographic Reference Service,
    using ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes, without remote foreign keys.

    Complete identification values are encrypted with authenticated encryption.
    Exact lookup and permanent identifier uniqueness use a tenant-isolated
    HMAC-SHA-256 fingerprint encoded as exactly 64 uppercase hexadecimal
    characters. Within one tenant and Identifier Scheme, the same normalized
    identifier value can never be registered more than once, regardless of
    lifecycle status.

    Identifier Schemes such as CEDULA, RUC and PASSPORT are database-managed
    reference data. Party Registry runtime reads them but does not create, update,
    delete or transition them through application use cases or REST endpoints.

    Keycloak authenticates accounts, but it is not the registry of persons.
    The relationship between an authenticated subject and party_id belongs to
    the Access Management Service.

    Every mutable business table contains created_at, created_by, updated_at and
    updated_by. Aggregate roots additionally contain version for optimistic
    concurrency control.

    party_outbox_events is infrastructure for reliable publication of tenant-scoped
    business events. It does not publish database-schema, Flyway, platform, or
    database-managed identifier-scheme catalog changes.
  '''
}

// Enums

Enum party_type {
  NATURAL_PERSON
  LEGAL_ENTITY
}

Enum party_record_status {
  DRAFT
  ACTIVE
  INACTIVE
  ARCHIVED
}

Enum identifier_category {
  NATIONAL_ID
  TAX_ID
  PASSPORT
  RESIDENCE_PERMIT
  LEGAL_REGISTRATION_NUMBER
  OTHER
}

Enum identifier_subject_type {
  NATURAL_PERSON
  LEGAL_ENTITY
  BOTH
}

Enum identifier_scheme_status {
  DRAFT
  ACTIVE
  DEPRECATED
  RETIRED
}

Enum party_identifier_status {
  PENDING_VERIFICATION
  VERIFIED
  REJECTED
  EXPIRED
  REVOKED
}

Enum party_outbox_aggregate_type {
  PARTY
  PARTY_IDENTIFIER
}

Enum outbox_status {
  PENDING
  PUBLISHED
  FAILED
}

// Tables

Table parties {
  id UUID [pk, not null, default: `uuidv7()`]
  tenant_id UUID [not null, note: 'Opaque reference to the tenant that owns this Party representation.']

  type party_type [not null]
  display_name VARCHAR(300) [not null, note: 'Canonical denormalized Party display name derived by Domain/Application from the corresponding detail row and persisted atomically.']
  record_status party_record_status [not null, default: 'DRAFT']

  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ [not null, default: `now()`]
  created_by VARCHAR(128) [not null, note: 'Opaque authenticated subject or service principal.']
  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ [not null, default: `now()`]
  updated_by VARCHAR(128) [not null, note: 'Opaque authenticated subject or service principal.']
  version BIGINT [not null, default: 0, note: 'Optimistic concurrency version of the Party aggregate.']

  indexes {
    (tenant_id, id) [unique, name: 'uq_parties_tenant_id']
    (tenant_id, type, record_status) [name: 'ix_parties_tenant_type_status']
    (tenant_id, display_name) [name: 'ix_parties_tenant_display_name']
  }

  checks {
    `version >= 0` [name: 'ck_parties_nonnegative_version']
  }

  Note: '''
    Root of the Party aggregate. A Party is either NATURAL_PERSON or LEGAL_ENTITY.
    It is never a Customer, Supplier, Employee, User, Tenant, or operating company.

    display_name is derived deterministically by Domain/Application:
    - NATURAL_PERSON: normalize given_names and family_names independently, then
      join them with exactly one ASCII U+0020 SPACE.
    - LEGAL_ENTITY: normalize legal_name.

    Name normalization trims leading and trailing whitespace and collapses each
    internal run of whitespace to exactly one ASCII U+0020 SPACE. Letter case and
    diacritics are preserved. preferred_name and trade_name never replace the
    canonical display_name in V1. A mutation to a source name field and its
    resulting display_name update must commit atomically in the same transaction.

    Any mutation to natural_person_details, legal_entity_details or
    party_nationalities must increment parties.version in the same transaction.
  '''
}

Table natural_person_details {
  party_id UUID [pk, not null]

  given_names VARCHAR(200) [not null]
  family_names VARCHAR(200) [not null]
  preferred_name VARCHAR(200)
  birth_date DATE
  date_of_death DATE
  birth_country_code CHAR(2) [note: 'ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code.']

  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ [not null, default: `now()`]
  created_by VARCHAR(128) [not null]
  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ [not null, default: `now()`]
  updated_by VARCHAR(128) [not null]

  checks {
    `date_of_death IS NULL OR birth_date IS NULL OR date_of_death >= birth_date` [name: 'ck_natural_person_life_dates']
    `birth_country_code IS NULL OR birth_country_code ~ '^[A-Z]{2}$'` [name: 'ck_natural_person_birth_country_code']
  }

  Note: '''
    One-to-one component of the Party aggregate for NATURAL_PERSON.

    Flyway must implement one deferred party/detail integrity mechanism using
    function fn_enforce_party_detail_type and these constraint-trigger objects:
    - ct_parties_detail_type on parties for INSERT and UPDATE of type.
    - ct_natural_person_details_party_type on natural_person_details for INSERT,
      UPDATE of party_id and DELETE.
    - ct_legal_entity_details_party_type on legal_entity_details for INSERT,
      UPDATE of party_id and DELETE.

    Each constraint trigger executes AFTER the stated row event, FOR EACH ROW,

Table natural_person_details {
  party_id UUID [pk, not null]

  given_names VARCHAR(200) [not null]
  family_names VARCHAR(200) [not null]
  preferred_name VARCHAR(200)
  birth_date DATE
  date_of_death DATE
  birth_country_code CHAR(2) [note: 'ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code.']

  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ [not null, default: `now()`]
  created_by VARCHAR(128) [not null]
  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ [not null, default: `now()`]
  updated_by VARCHAR(128) [not null]

  checks {
    `date_of_death IS NULL OR birth_date IS NULL OR date_of_death >= birth_date` [name: 'ck_natural_person_life_dates']
    `birth_country_code IS NULL OR birth_country_code ~ '^[A-Z]{2}$'` [name: 'ck_natural_person_birth_country_code']
  }

  Note: '''
    One-to-one component of the Party aggregate for NATURAL_PERSON.

    Flyway must implement one deferred party/detail integrity mechanism using
    function fn_enforce_party_detail_type and these constraint-trigger objects:
    - ct_parties_detail_type on parties for INSERT and UPDATE of type.
    - ct_natural_person_details_party_type on natural_person_details for INSERT,
      UPDATE of party_id and DELETE.
    - ct_legal_entity_details_party_type on legal_entity_details for INSERT,
      UPDATE of party_id and DELETE.

    Each constraint trigger executes AFTER the stated row event, FOR EACH ROW,
    DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED, so the invariant is evaluated at transaction
    commit after Party and detail rows may have been written in either order.

    At commit, each affected Party must satisfy exactly one detail invariant:
    - NATURAL_PERSON has exactly one natural_person_details row and zero
      legal_entity_details rows.
    - LEGAL_ENTITY has exactly one legal_entity_details row and zero
      natural_person_details rows.

    The Flyway migration and PostgreSQL integration tests must prove both valid
    insertion orderings in one transaction and must reject a missing required
    detail, a type-incompatible detail, both detail types for one Party, and any
    update/delete that would leave the committed invariant invalid.
  '''
}

Table legal_entity_details {
  party_id UUID [pk, not null]

  legal_name VARCHAR(300) [not null, note: 'Official registered name.']
  trade_name VARCHAR(300) [note: 'Primary trade name for V1; it does not replace legal_name.']
  legal_form_code VARCHAR(64) [note: 'Jurisdiction-qualified code, for example EC_SAS, EC_SA or US_LLC.']
  incorporation_country_code CHAR(2) [not null, note: 'ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code.']
  incorporated_on DATE
  dissolved_on DATE

  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ [not null, default: `now()`]
  created_by VARCHAR(128) [not null]
  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ [not null, default: `now()`]
  updated_by VARCHAR(128) [not null]

  checks {
    `dissolved_on IS NULL OR incorporated_on IS NULL OR dissolved_on >= incorporated_on` [name: 'ck_legal_entity_lifecycle_dates']
    `incorporation_country_code ~ '^[A-Z]{2}$'` [name: 'ck_legal_entity_incorporation_country_code']
  }

  Note: '''
    One-to-one component of the Party aggregate for LEGAL_ENTITY.
    It does not represent tenant configuration, tax configuration, ownership,
    corporate hierarchy, or commercial roles.
  '''
}

Table party_nationalities {
  id UUID [pk, not null, default: `uuidv7()`]
  party_id UUID [not null]

  country_code CHAR(2) [not null, note: 'ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code.']
  is_primary BOOLEAN [not null, default: false]
  valid_from DATE
  valid_until DATE

  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ [not null, default: `now()`]
  created_by VARCHAR(128) [not null]
  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ [not null, default: `now()`]
  updated_by VARCHAR(128) [not null]

  indexes {
    (party_id, country_code) [name: 'ix_party_nationalities_country']
    (party_id, is_primary) [name: 'ix_party_nationalities_primary']
  }

  checks {
    `country_code ~ '^[A-Z]{2}$'` [name: 'ck_party_nationality_country_code']
    `valid_until IS NULL OR valid_from IS NULL OR valid_until >= valid_from` [name: 'ck_party_nationality_validity']
  }

  Note: '''
    Nationalities known and maintained by the tenant for a natural-person Party.

    party_nationalities intentionally does not duplicate tenant_id. party_id
    references the globally unique parties.id, so the owning tenant is inherited
    unambiguously through that Party relationship.

    Flyway must create these exact partial unique indexes:
    - uq_party_nationalities_active_country on (party_id, country_code)
      WHERE valid_until IS NULL.
    - uq_party_nationalities_active_primary on (party_id)

134: ## 6. Strict Clean Architecture
135: 
136: ### 6.1 Logical areas
137: 
138: | Area | Responsibilities | Forbidden dependencies |
139: |---|---|---|
140: | Domain | Entities/value objects, Party/Identifier lifecycle policies, invariants, masking and business errors. | Quarkus, Jakarta, CDI, REST, JSON, logging, ORM/Panache, database, messaging, configuration, crypto-provider APIs. |
141: | Application | Party and Identifier commands/queries, input ports, use cases, transaction intent, tenant scoping, read-only Scheme catalog contract, output ports and boundary-neutral outcomes. | Concrete adapters, REST/persistence/provider DTOs, Quarkus APIs, MDC/SLF4J. |
142: | Inbound adapters | Reactive REST parsing, request context, DTO mapping, ETag/If-Match, ApiResponse/error mapping. | Business-rule ownership, direct DB/client access, Scheme catalog administration. |
143: | Outbound adapters | PostgreSQL, Geographic client/cache, runtime-secret crypto, RabbitMQ, local structured security logging, clock. | Redefining domain rules or exposing adapter models inward. |
144: | Bootstrap | Quarkus wiring/configuration, adapter selection, runtime privilege/config validation, startup/readiness and telemetry setup. | Business decisions. |
145: 
146: ### 6.2 Application ports
147: 
148: | Port | Direction | Responsibility |
149: |---|---|---|
150: | Party use-case ports | Inbound | Party/detail/nationality approved commands and queries. |
151: | Party Identifier use-case ports | Inbound | Identifier lifecycle, lookup, exact search and decryption. |
152: | Identifier Scheme catalog port | Outbound, read-only | Read database-managed Scheme metadata needed by Party Identifier processing. It exposes queries only. |
153: | Tenant-scoped persistence ports | Outbound | Tenant-qualified Party/Identifier reads and mutations; no persistence model leakage. |
154: | Unit-of-work/outbox port | Outbound | Commit represented business mutation and required outbox row atomically. |
155: | Geographic reference port | Outbound | Resolve active country references with explicit availability outcomes. |
156: | Identifier protection port | Outbound | Authenticated encryption/decryption and tenant-effective HMAC using runtime secrets. |
157: | Integration event publisher port | Outbound | Publish persistent versioned messages and classify publisher confirms. |
158: | Decryption security-log port | Outbound | Emit required non-plaintext local structured log before plaintext return. |
159: | Clock port | Outbound | Testable current time; no scheduler is implied. |
160: 
161: There is intentionally **no Scheme Administration input port**, no Scheme mutation port and no Party-creation idempotency port.
162: 
163: ### 6.3 Explicit core ownership and dependency direction
164: 
165: The LikeC4 component view represents the core boundaries as first-class elements rather than leaving them implicit in relationship text:
166: 
167: - `partyDomain` is the framework-independent Domain component.
168: - `partyCapability` and `identifierCapability` are Application-layer use-case components.
169: - `partyInputPorts` and `identifierInputPorts` are Application-owned input-port components.
170: - `partyPersistencePorts`, `identifierPersistencePorts`, `geographicReferencePort`, `identifierProtectionPort`, `securityLogPort`, `outboxStorePort`, `eventPublisherPort`, and `clockPort` are Application-owned output-port components.
171: - REST, PostgreSQL, Geographic Reference, protection, local logging, and RabbitMQ components are adapters that depend inward on those core-owned contracts.
172: - `runtimeComposition` is the Bootstrap boundary and alone selects and wires concrete adapters.
173: 
174: The directional rules are: inbound adapter → input port → application use case → domain; application use cases invoke output-port contracts; outbound adapters → output ports because adapters implement core-owned contracts; bootstrap → concrete runtime elements for composition. No Domain or Application element depends on an adapter or framework. Runtime call direction through an output port does not reverse compile-time ownership: the port remains defined by the Application core and the adapter imports/implements it.
175: 
176: ## 7. Database-Managed Identifier Scheme Catalog
177: 
178: ### 7.1 Ownership
179: 
180: `identifier_schemes` contains global reference metadata for supported official-document schemes such as CÉDULA, RUC and PASAPORTE.
181: 
182: The application runtime uses this table only to read the metadata required for Party Identifier processing:
183: 
184: - scheme identity/code;
185: - issuing country/category;
186: - applicable subject type;
187: - normalizer implementation key;
188: - validator implementation key;
189: - minimum/maximum length;
190: - expiration requirement;
191: - persisted status/usable-state metadata;
192: - version/audit metadata where required for diagnostics/contract validation.
193: 
194: ### 7.2 No runtime administration
195: 
196: Party Registry V1 exposes no REST/application operation to:
197: 
198: - create schemes;
199: - update schemes;
200: - activate/deprecate/retire schemes;
201: - delete schemes;
202: - search/browse schemes as an administration resource.
203: 
204: The presence of the DBML table does not imply CRUD.
205: 
206: New or changed Scheme data is delivered only through the governed database-management path: reviewed database migrations and/or explicitly authorized database administration.
207: 
208: ### 7.3 Runtime database privilege boundary
209: 
210: The runtime PostgreSQL role should enforce:
211: 
212: ```text
213: identifier_schemes
214:   SELECT: allowed
215:   INSERT: denied
216:   UPDATE: denied
217:   DELETE: denied
218: ```
219: 
220: Migration/database-administration credentials are separate from runtime credentials.
221: 
222: This privilege separation is mandatory architecture/database validation evidence. Application repositories/adapters must not expose Scheme mutation methods even if a broader development database account could technically execute them.
223: 
224: ### 7.4 Rule implementation compatibility
225: 
226: Normalizer/validator implementations remain versioned application code. A database-managed Scheme can reference only keys supported by the released application version.
227: 
228: If required persisted Scheme configuration references an unavailable implementation:
229: 
230: - dependent Party Identifier operations fail unchanged;
231: - readiness reflects unusable required configuration where applicable;
232: - the application does not mutate/repair the Scheme row.
233: 
234: A new Scheme that requires a new normalizer/validator therefore requires coordinated software release plus governed database change.
235: 
236: ## 8. Permanent Party Identifier Uniqueness
237: 
238: The business uniqueness scope is:
239: 
240: ```text
241: tenant + Identifier Scheme + normalized identifier value
242: ```
243: 
244: Since plaintext cannot be persisted, PostgreSQL enforces:
245: 
246: ```text
247: UNIQUE (tenant_id, identifier_scheme_id, normalized_value_hash)
248: ```
249: 
250: `normalized_value_hash` is the tenant-effective HMAC-SHA-256 of the normalized identifier.
251: 
252: The key is permanent across `PENDING_VERIFICATION`, `VERIFIED`, `REJECTED`, `EXPIRED` and `REVOKED`. Status never releases a document number for reuse inside the same tenant and Scheme.
253: 
254: The same normalized value may exist under another tenant or another Identifier Scheme.
255: 
256: Concurrent duplicates are resolved by the PostgreSQL unique constraint: at most one Party Identifier row commits. The losing operation returns the API `CONFLICT` category and creates no duplicate identifier/outbox side effect. This is business uniqueness, not command-response idempotency.
257: 
258: ## 9. Runtime Components
259: 
260: Stable component responsibilities are:
261: 
262: - **Domain:** Party Registry Domain.
263: - **Application use cases:** Party Application Capability, Identifier Application Capability, and Outbox Publication Capability.
264: - **Application-owned input ports:** Party Input Ports and Identifier Input Ports.
265: - **Application-owned output ports:** Party Persistence and Unit-of-Work Ports, Identifier and Scheme Catalog Ports, Geographic Reference Port, Identifier Protection Port, Decryption Security Log Port, Outbox Store Port, Event Publisher Port, and Clock Port.
266: - **Inbound adapter:** Reactive REST Adapter.
267: - **Outbound adapters:** PostgreSQL Adapter, Geographic Reference Adapter/cache, Identifier Protection Adapter, RabbitMQ Publisher Adapter, Decryption Security Log Adapter, and System Clock Adapter.
268: - **Bootstrap:** Runtime Composition and Readiness.
269: 
270: There is no Scheme Administration Capability. Scheme reads occur as part of Identifier processing through the read-only catalog port implemented by the PostgreSQL adapter.
271: 
272: ## 10. API Surface
273: 
274: The V1 REST API is rooted under `/api/v1` and follows the approved ApiResponse/ETag/If-Match conventions.
275: 
276: Runtime REST surface includes approved Party, Party-detail, nationality and Party Identifier operations.
277: 
278: The API MUST NOT expose Identifier Scheme administration. Amendment 002 also removes the previously generated Scheme lookup/search resources from V1; runtime Scheme access is internal reference-data access unless a later explicit requirement introduces a read-only public/internal discovery contract.
279: 
280: No `Idempotency-Key` is accepted or interpreted by V1 commands.
281: 
282: RG-401 remains a nonblocking downstream API-contract authority issue for exact pagination/filter/sort defaults. Architecture does not manufacture those values.
283: 
284: ### 10.1 Contract-first rule
285: 
286: The OpenAPI document is the downstream source of truth for the detailed HTTPS/JSON contract and is owned by Party Registry; internal consumers are its consumers. It must version the `/api/v1` surface, preserve `ApiResponse`, context, ETag/If-Match, error, masking, no-store, and tenant non-disclosure semantics, and exclude Scheme administration, outbox CRUD, command idempotency, stack traces, and plaintext outside the decryption response. Published V1 meanings are backward compatible; an incompatible change requires a new approved contract version. Transport DTOs remain inside the inbound adapter and are mapped to boundary-neutral application inputs/results.
287: 
288: ## 11. Transaction Boundaries
289: 
290: | Flow | Atomicity / behavior |
291: |---|---|
292: | Party creation | Local transaction creates Party/approved initial data and required Party outbox event. |
293: | Party/detail/nationality mutation | Local transaction updates component, Party version, audit facts and required outbox event. |
294: | Party Identifier creation/mutation | Local transaction preserves tenant/Party/Scheme invariants, permanent uniqueness, version/audit state and required outbox event. |
295: | Identifier Scheme access | Read-only query of database-managed reference data; no business mutation transaction exists. |
296: | Outbox delivery | A short claim transaction reserves eligible rows using only DBML fields and commits before broker I/O; publication occurs with no open database transaction or row lock; a separate outcome transaction records confirmation/failure. |
297: | Exact identifier search | Tenant+Scheme HMAC lookup; no decrypt/scan. |
298: | Decryption | Tenant-qualified read -> ciphertext authentication/decrypt -> required local security log -> no-store plaintext response. |
299: 
300: There is no Scheme mutation flow, no distributed transaction, no saga and no compensation design.
301: 
302: For every country-dependent state change, Geographic Reference resolution (including cache lookup and any remote call) completes **before** the state-changing PostgreSQL transaction begins. The application first obtains usable country evidence or returns the approved unchanged 503 outcome. Only after evidence is available may it open the local mutation/outbox transaction; the evidence is then consumed without another remote call inside that transaction. Every other remote interaction likewise occurs outside state-changing PostgreSQL transactions. RabbitMQ follows the separately committed claim/broker/outcome boundaries in section 12.2. No database connection transaction or row lock is held while awaiting Geographic Reference, RabbitMQ, or any other remote system.
303: 
304: ## 12. Transactional Outbox
305: 
306: Approved Party and Party Identifier mutations that require events commit the business mutation and outbox insertion in the same PostgreSQL transaction.
307: 
308: Publisher semantics remain:
309: 
310: - persistent RabbitMQ messages;
311: - publisher confirms;
312: - at-least-once delivery;
313: - same event ID on retry/recovery;
314: - transient/unknown outcomes remain retryable;

### 6.3 Explicit core ownership and dependency direction

The LikeC4 component view represents the core boundaries as first-class elements rather than leaving them implicit in relationship text:

- `partyDomain` is the framework-independent Domain component.
- `partyCapability` and `identifierCapability` are Application-layer use-case components.
- `partyInputPorts` and `identifierInputPorts` are Application-owned input-port components.
- `partyPersistencePorts`, `identifierPersistencePorts`, `geographicReferencePort`, `identifierProtectionPort`, `securityLogPort`, `outboxStorePort`, `eventPublisherPort`, and `clockPort` are Application-owned output-port components.

- applicable subject type;
- normalizer implementation key;
- validator implementation key;
- minimum/maximum length;
- expiration requirement;
- persisted status/usable-state metadata;
- version/audit metadata where required for diagnostics/contract validation.

### 7.2 No runtime administration

Party Registry V1 exposes no REST/application operation to:

- create schemes;
- update schemes;
- activate/deprecate/retire schemes;
- delete schemes;
- search/browse schemes as an administration resource.

The presence of the DBML table does not imply CRUD.

New or changed Scheme data is delivered only through the governed database-management path: reviewed database migrations and/or explicitly authorized database administration.

### 7.3 Runtime database privilege boundary

The runtime PostgreSQL role should enforce:

```text
identifier_schemes
  SELECT: allowed
  INSERT: denied
  UPDATE: denied
  DELETE: denied
```

Migration/database-administration credentials are separate from runtime credentials.

This privilege separation is mandatory architecture/database validation evidence. Application repositories/adapters must not expose Scheme mutation methods even if a broader development database account could technically execute them.

### 7.4 Rule implementation compatibility

Normalizer/validator implementations remain versioned application code. A database-managed Scheme can reference only keys supported by the released application version.

If required persisted Scheme configuration references an unavailable implementation:

- dependent Party Identifier operations fail unchanged;
- readiness reflects unusable required configuration where applicable;
- the application does not mutate/repair the Scheme row.

A new Scheme that requires a new normalizer/validator therefore requires coordinated software release plus governed database change.

## 8. Permanent Party Identifier Uniqueness

The business uniqueness scope is:

```text
tenant + Identifier Scheme + normalized identifier value
```

Since plaintext cannot be persisted, PostgreSQL enforces:

```text
UNIQUE (tenant_id, identifier_scheme_id, normalized_value_hash)
```

`normalized_value_hash` is the tenant-effective HMAC-SHA-256 of the normalized identifier.

The key is permanent across `PENDING_VERIFICATION`, `VERIFIED`, `REJECTED`, `EXPIRED` and `REVOKED`. Status never releases a document number for reuse inside the same tenant and Scheme.

The same normalized value may exist under another tenant or another Identifier Scheme.

Concurrent duplicates are resolved by the PostgreSQL unique constraint: at most one Party Identifier row commits. The losing operation returns the API `CONFLICT` category and creates no duplicate identifier/outbox side effect. This is business uniqueness, not command-response idempotency.

Stable component responsibilities are:

- **Domain:** Party Registry Domain.
- **Application use cases:** Party Application Capability, Identifier Application Capability, and Outbox Publication Capability.
- **Application-owned input ports:** Party Input Ports and Identifier Input Ports.
- **Application-owned output ports:** Party Persistence and Unit-of-Work Ports, Identifier and Scheme Catalog Ports, Geographic Reference Port, Identifier Protection Port, Decryption Security Log Port, Outbox Store Port, Event Publisher Port, and Clock Port.
- **Inbound adapter:** Reactive REST Adapter.
- **Outbound adapters:** PostgreSQL Adapter, Geographic Reference Adapter/cache, Identifier Protection Adapter, RabbitMQ Publisher Adapter, Decryption Security Log Adapter, and System Clock Adapter.
- **Bootstrap:** Runtime Composition and Readiness.

There is no Scheme Administration Capability. Scheme reads occur as part of Identifier processing through the read-only catalog port implemented by the PostgreSQL adapter.

## 10. API Surface

The V1 REST API is rooted under `/api/v1` and follows the approved ApiResponse/ETag/If-Match conventions.

Runtime REST surface includes approved Party, Party-detail, nationality and Party Identifier operations.

The API MUST NOT expose Identifier Scheme administration. Amendment 002 also removes the previously generated Scheme lookup/search resources from V1; runtime Scheme access is internal reference-data access unless a later explicit requirement introduces a read-only public/internal discovery contract.

No `Idempotency-Key` is accepted or interpreted by V1 commands.

RG-401 remains a nonblocking downstream API-contract authority issue for exact pagination/filter/sort defaults. Architecture does not manufacture those values.

### 10.1 Contract-first rule

The OpenAPI document is the downstream source of truth for the detailed HTTPS/JSON contract and is owned by Party Registry; internal consumers are its consumers. It must version the `/api/v1` surface, preserve `ApiResponse`, context, ETag/If-Match, error, masking, no-store, and tenant non-disclosure semantics, and exclude Scheme administration, outbox CRUD, command idempotency, stack traces, and plaintext outside the decryption response. Published V1 meanings are backward compatible; an incompatible change requires a new approved contract version. Transport DTOs remain inside the inbound adapter and are mapped to boundary-neutral application inputs/results.

## 11. Transaction Boundaries

| Flow | Atomicity / behavior |
|---|---|
| Party creation | Local transaction creates Party/approved initial data and required Party outbox event. |
| Party/detail/nationality mutation | Local transaction updates component, Party version, audit facts and required outbox event. |
| Party Identifier creation/mutation | Local transaction preserves tenant/Party/Scheme invariants, permanent uniqueness, version/audit state and required outbox event. |
| Identifier Scheme access | Read-only query of database-managed reference data; no business mutation transaction exists. |
| Outbox delivery | A short claim transaction reserves eligible rows using only DBML fields and commits before broker I/O; publication occurs with no open database transaction or row lock; a separate outcome transaction records confirmation/failure. |
| Exact identifier search | Tenant+Scheme HMAC lookup; no decrypt/scan. |
| Decryption | Tenant-qualified read -> ciphertext authentication/decrypt -> required local security log -> no-store plaintext response. |

There is no Scheme mutation flow, no distributed transaction, no saga and no compensation design.

For every country-dependent state change, Geographic Reference resolution (including cache lookup and any remote call) completes **before** the state-changing PostgreSQL transaction begins. The application first obtains usable country evidence or returns the approved unchanged 503 outcome. Only after evidence is available may it open the local mutation/outbox transaction; the evidence is then consumed without another remote call inside that transaction. Every other remote interaction likewise occurs outside state-changing PostgreSQL transactions. RabbitMQ follows the separately committed claim/broker/outcome boundaries in section 12.2. No database connection transaction or row lock is held while awaiting Geographic Reference, RabbitMQ, or any other remote system.

## 12. Transactional Outbox

Approved Party and Party Identifier mutations that require events commit the business mutation and outbox insertion in the same PostgreSQL transaction.

Publisher semantics remain:

- persistent RabbitMQ messages;
- publisher confirms;
- at-least-once delivery;
- same event ID on retry/recovery;
- transient/unknown outcomes remain retryable;

+# Party canonical display-name flow — T040
+
+This is the test-first Domain/Application flow contract for T041 and the later PostgreSQL adapter task. It maps frozen OpenAPI names to the final DBML while remaining neutral about transport DTOs, persistence records, SQL, constructors and database defaults. Canonical derivation is exclusively the existing `DisplayName` domain policy.
+
+## Source and mutation flow
+
+| Scenario / authority | OpenAPI source | Domain rule and DBML destination | Required boundary-neutral application flow | T040 assertion |
+|---|---|---|---|---|
+| Natural-person create; FR-002/010/016, AC-002/030/036 | `type=NATURAL_PERSON`; `details.kind=NATURAL_PERSON`; `givenNames`, `familyNames`; nullable `preferredName` | `DisplayName.forNaturalPerson(givenNames, familyNames)` -> `parties.display_name`; source values -> `natural_person_details.given_names/family_names`; `preferred_name` is never substituted | Matching Party type, detail kind, unchanged source details and exact canonical value travel in one Party mutation intent to one `createPartyAndAppendOutbox` call | `naturalPersonCreationCarriesCanonicalNameAndMatchingSourcesInOneAtomicIntent` asserts trim/collapse, case/diacritics, source values, preferred-name exclusion and one call |
+| Legal-entity create; FR-002/010/016, AC-002/030/036 | `type=LEGAL_ENTITY`; `details.kind=LEGAL_ENTITY`; `legalName`; nullable `tradeName` | `DisplayName.forLegalEntity(legalName)` -> `parties.display_name`; source -> `legal_entity_details.legal_name`; `trade_name` is never substituted | Matching Party type, detail kind, unchanged source detail and exact canonical value travel together in the same create intent | `legalEntityCreationCarriesCanonicalLegalNameWithoutSubstitutingTradeName` asserts trim/collapse, case/diacritics, trade-name exclusion and one call |
+| Natural-person detail-name update; FR-021/028, AC-031/038/070 | `kind=NATURAL_PERSON`; `givenNames`, `familyNames`; nullable `preferredName` | The same natural-person policy derives `parties.display_name`; source detail and display name commit atomically per DBML lines 133-145 | Detail kind, source values, canonical value and expected Party version travel together in one update intent | `naturalPersonDetailNameUpdateCarriesCanonicalNameSourcesVersionAndOutboxTogether` |
+| Legal-entity detail-name update; FR-021/028, AC-031/038/070 | `kind=LEGAL_ENTITY`; `legalName`; nullable `tradeName` | The same legal-entity policy derives `parties.display_name`; legal name and display name commit atomically | Detail kind, legal source, canonical value and expected Party version travel together in one update intent | `legalEntityDetailNameUpdateCarriesCanonicalLegalNameWithoutSubstitutingTradeName` |
+| Type/detail consistency; FR-002/016, DR-002, AC-002/036 | Party create discriminator requires matching `type` and `details.kind` | A Party has exactly one matching DBML detail kind | Both mismatch directions are rejected before `PartyUnitOfWorkPort`; an adapter never selects or repairs the kind | `creationRejectsBothTypeDetailMismatchesWithoutAUnitOfWorkCall` |
+| Required canonical sources; OpenAPI `minLength: 1`; DBML `NOT NULL`; approved `DisplayName` policy | Natural person requires `givenNames` and `familyNames`; legal entity requires `legalName` | Null/blank sources are rejected by the existing policy; no second normalizer is permitted | Derivation occurs before persistence; blank given names, family names or legal name produce zero unit-of-work calls | `creationRejectsBlankNaturalPersonDisplayNameSourcesBeforePersistence`; `detailUpdateRejectsBlankLegalNameBeforePersistence` |
+| Tenant and audit; FR-007/011, DR-005, AC-011/019 | Valid request-context headers (outside body) | `parties.tenant_id`, `created_by`/`updated_by` and matching detail audit fields | `RequestContext.tenantId/userId` remain the intent tenant and actor; no adapter default | All four success tests assert the exact synthetic tenant and actor at the unit-of-work boundary |
+| Version; FR-012/021/028, AC-020/031/038/070 | `If-Match` is outside the body | `parties.version`; detail mutation increments it in the same transaction | Creation carries expected version `0`; updates carry supplied version `7`; canonical and source details share that intent | All create/update success tests assert exact expected version and one atomic call |
+| Geography ordering; FR-015, VR-002, AC-004/023; architecture section 11 | `birthCountryCode` / `incorporationCountryCode` | Country remains the matching detail column; no remote call occurs in the database transaction | `GeographicReferencePort.resolveActive` completes before `PartyUnitOfWorkPort` invocation | All four success tests assert the shared call sequence exactly |
+| Outbox identity and atomicity; VR-006, NFR-002, AC-012 | No transport field invents event identity | Party/detail/display-name/version/audit mutation and one outbox row are one transaction | Existing event types remain `party.created.v1` and `party.updated.v1`; request `processId` remains correlation identity on the same mutation intent | All four success tests assert event type, correlation UUID, method call count and absence of a second Party unit-of-work operation |
+
+## Triggering T012 finding closure contract
+
+| Current T012 finding | Meaningful red assertion | Flow-map rows |
+|---|---|---|
+| `PartyMutationIntent` has no canonical display-name carrier | Each successful create/update spy searches the one boundary-neutral intent for `canonicalDisplayName` or `displayName` and compares it to the exact existing domain-policy result | Four create/update scenario rows |
+| `CreatePartyUseCase` sends the unprocessed command | Create spies require canonical value together with Party type, matching detail kind, unchanged source details, tenant, actor, version and outbox identity | Natural-person create; legal-entity create; tenant/audit; version; outbox rows |
+| `UpdatePartyDetailsUseCase` sends raw details | Update spies require canonical value together with matching source details and expected aggregate version in the same unit-of-work argument | Both detail update; version; outbox rows |

+| Source-name and display-name updates must be atomic | Each success case permits exactly one mutation-and-outbox port call and inspects source, canonical, tenant, version, actor and outbox facts in that call | Version and outbox/atomicity rows |
